text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 index ended practically unchanged as profit-taking in the U.S. and in the British gilt market deflated an early rally that had propelled blue chips to a record peak. The leading British share index ended 0.1 point lower at 4,307.7.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade sharply higher, just shy of the 3,200-point level as the market shrugged off the impact of a slightly weaker dollar to advance strongly, trade underpinned by firm close on Wall Street on Friday. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,184.36 up 46.35 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,185.72.

PARIS - French shares closed with narrow losses, after trading most of the day in positive territory, a slightly softer Wall Street took the shine off Paris stocks but the market was generally well supported, with fresh money pouring in as investors who missed January's bull run attempt to catch up. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 2.15 points or 0.08 percent to 2,595.37.

ZURICH - Swiss shares powered to their eighth consecutive record close after overcoming a tentative start as firming bond prices gave shares a boost. In the current bullish environment, even laggards such as stocks of Swiss retailers saw interest. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) climbed 12.88 points or 0.46 percent to 2,796.13.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed higher as the yen's weakness against the dollar eased worries that a rebound in the yen after the weekend Group of Seven (G7) meeting might pull down major export-oriented shares that have recently acted as a prop for the market. The key 225-share Nikkei average gained 314.13 points or 1.76 percent to close at 18,181.17.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks edged to a slightly lower close, but brokers said the index would have been harder hit without the strength in finance issues, particularly HSBC Holdings. The Hang Seng Index slipped 16.96 points or 0.12 percent to 13,643.54.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended mixed, losing ground in late trade as investors focused on negative sentiment surrounding metal prices and the local currency, having scaled fresh heights early, the thinly-dealt market tumbled back just as quickly as mining stocks were mauled on concerns over commodity prices and the Australian dollar. The All Ordinaries index lost 0.3 points to close at 2,446.4.

JOHANNESBURG - A host of bullish factors powered industrial shares sharply higher as golds continued to sag on a struggling bullion price, bullish January reserves data and a stronger Wall Street on Friday, coupled with a firmer rand and strong long bonds on Monday helped the market extend its Friday gains in busy trade. The Overall index added 76.4 points to 6,956.0, the Industrial index rose 83.5 points to 8,286.5, and the Gold index lost 7.1 points to 1,350.4.
